mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months indicates contracting manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings for industrial firms and drags the S&P 500 lower over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual shock of monetary tightening and inflation, which erodes real purchasing power and depresses equity valuations over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both above 12-month moving average
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a broad-based collapse in demand, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both fall > -1% MoM
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average, combined with a stable unemployment rate, signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS above 12-month moving average and UNRATE stable
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive correlation exists between industrial production growth (INDPRO) and S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days, as improving manufacturing activity quickly boosts earnings expectations.
failure_condition: The correlation between INDPRO monthly change and S&P 500 5-day forward returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) in out-of-sample tests.
